titleEn: Fall From Ladder - Spinal Injury With Wrist Fracture

patient.name: Mark
patient.affectEn: alert and cooperative but frightened; lying very still on his back with his eyes open, deliberately not moving his head; winces whenever the right wrist is touched or bumped
patient.speechEn: full, clear sentences; keeps his head perfectly still while talking; answers every question readily and asks whether his neck is broken

scene.settingEn: Backyard concrete patio of a single-storey house in Burnaby, reached through a side gate. An aluminum extension ladder lies on its side, clear of the patient. The patient is supine on the concrete where he landed and has NOT been moved. His wife kneels beside him. Overcast, 14 degrees C, dry. One patient. The gutter line he fell from is approximately 4 metres above the ground.
hazardsEn: aluminum extension ladder lying on its side, clear of the patient
hard concrete patio surface (landing surface and working surface)
no other hazards: scene is dry, overcast, 14 degrees C; no electrical, traffic or animal hazards

bystanders.knowsEn: watched him fall: the ladder feet slipped while he was cleaning the gutters, he fell straight down about 4 m and landed flat on his back on the concrete; his head did not hit; he did not pass out; he has not moved since; she called 911

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: spinal immobilization device (long spine board or scoop stretcher)
hard cervical collars in all adult sizes
head blocks (foam rollers) and spinal straps
splint kit (padded board splints or malleable splints) with padding and roller bandages
oxygen kit with nasal cannula and non-rebreather mask
Entonox cylinder with demand valve and mouthpiece
PCP oral analgesia kit: acetaminophen and ibuprofen tablets

dispatchEn: 1410 hrs. Code 3 to a single-storey residence in Burnaby. 34-year-old male fell from a ladder while cleaning gutters. Caller (his wife) reports he is conscious, lying on the back patio, complaining of neck pain. Fire is not attending. Closest hospital is 15 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: You and your partner are a BLS crew. Travel time to scene is 8 minutes. No update from dispatch en route.
arrivalEn: His wife meets you at the side gate and leads you through to the back patio. The ladder lies on its side, clear of the patient. Mark is supine on the concrete where he landed; his wife says he has not been moved. She kneels beside him.
firstLookEn: Adult male supine on the concrete, eyes open, holding very still and speaking to his wife in full sentences. Obvious deformity of the right wrist. No visible bleeding.

primary.locEn: Alert. Oriented to person, place, time and event. Answers in full sentences and follows commands.
primary.airwayEn: Open, clear and self-maintained; he is speaking in full sentences. No blood, fluid or foreign material in the mouth.
primary.breathingEn: 18 per minute, regular, good volume, equal chest rise, no distress or accessory muscle use. SpO2 97% on room air if checked now.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 92, strong and regular. No external bleeding found.
primary.rbsEn: Head and neck: midline cervical tenderness at C5-C6 when palpated; no deformity. Chest, abdomen, pelvis, legs: no injuries. Right arm: when exposed, the right wrist is dorsally deformed and swollen; distal circulation, sensation and function (CSM) INTACT; no open wound. Left arm unremarkable. No bleeding anywhere. Skin pink, warm, dry (skin is given automatically during the RBS).

history.ccEn: It is my neck - right in the middle at the back - and my right wrist. The wrist hurts more, but it is the neck I am scared about. I do not want to move my head.

opqrst.oEn: It started the moment I hit the ground. I was up the ladder cleaning the gutters and the feet of the ladder slipped out. I fell straight down, about 4 metres, and landed flat on my back on the concrete. My head did not hit. I never blacked out, and I have not moved since I landed.
opqrst.pEn: Any time I try to move my head the neck pain gets worse, so I am keeping dead still. The wrist hurts more whenever anything touches it or I try to move my hand. Nothing makes either one better.
opqrst.qEn: The neck is a deep, steady ache. The wrist is sharp.
opqrst.rEn: The neck pain stays in my neck - it does not go down my arms, into my back or anywhere else. The wrist pain is just at the wrist. Neither has come and gone; it has been there the whole time.
opqrst.sEn: The neck is about 5 out of 10. The wrist is a 7 out of 10.
opqrst.tEn: Since the fall - it has been constant since I landed, and it has not changed.

history.painScoreEn: Neck 5/10; right wrist 7/10. After analgesia (vitals set 2): neck 3/10, wrist 3/10.

sample.sEn: Neck pain and right wrist pain. Nothing else that I have noticed.
sample.aEn: No allergies that I know of.
sample.mEn: I do not take any medications - nothing prescribed, nothing over the counter.
sample.pEn: Nothing. I am healthy, no medical problems, never been in hospital.
sample.lEn: A sandwich and a coffee about an hour ago.
sample.eEn: I was up the ladder cleaning the gutters and the feet slipped out from under me. Free fall, landed flat on my back on the concrete. My wife saw the whole thing.

fe.generalEn: I am healthy. No recent illness, no colds, nothing.
fe.cnsEn: No headache, no dizziness. No numbness, no tingling, no weakness anywhere - I can feel and move my fingers and my toes on both sides.
fe.respiratoryEn: No shortness of breath. Breathing feels normal.
fe.giGuEn: No belly pain, no nausea. I have not lost control of my bladder or bowels.
fe.integumentaryEn: Nothing except the swelling at my wrist. No rashes, no other cuts or bruises that I know of.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: Just the neck and the right wrist. Nothing else hurts.
fe.eentEn: My vision is fine, no double vision. Nothing coming out of my ears or nose, no blood.

findings.headNeckEn: Midline tenderness at C5-C6 on palpation; no deformity or step-off. No DOTS to the scalp or face. No blood or fluid from the ears or nose. Mouth clear.
findings.chestLungsEn: No DOTS. Equal chest rise. Air entry equal with clear breath sounds in all 6 auscultation sites, through inspiration and expiration.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft and non-tender in all four quadrants. No DOTS.
findings.backEn: Assessed during the coordinated roll onto the spinal device, alignment maintained: no thoracolumbar tenderness or deformity, no DOTS.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No injury to the pelvis or either leg. Distal CSM intact bilaterally.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Right wrist: dorsal deformity and swelling as found on the RBS; distal circulation, sensation and function intact. Left arm unremarkable, CSM intact. CSM equal when both hands are compared.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge dispatch and plan equipment: spinal device, hard collars, splint kit, oxygen, analgesia kit
triggers: we will bring the spine board
grab the collars and splint kit
bring the oxygen and the Entonox
ladder fall so I am planning spinal gear

expected.actionEn: Anticipate hazards (ladder, wet surfaces) and PPE needs before arrival
triggers: ladder could still be a hazard
gloves and glasses on before we go in
thinking about scene safety en route
could be a fall from height

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards, environment, MOI (approx. 4 m fall onto concrete) and number of patients (1) before touching the patient
triggers: ladder is clear of the patient
mechanism is a fall of about 4 metres onto concrete

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection
First-look visual assessment: patient supine, eyes open, holding very still, obvious right wrist deformity
triggers: what does the patient look like
he is lying still with his eyes open
I can see the wrist is deformed

expected.actionEn: Assess LOC and verbalize placement on AVPU: Alert
triggers: can you hear me, what is your name

expected.actionEn: Take manual in-line c-spine control BEFORE any movement or pain stimulus (MOI plus midline neck pain = NEXUS positive)
triggers: NEXUS positive so I am controlling the neck

expected.actionEn: Assess airway patency
triggers: he is talking so the airway is patent

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing rate, depth and effort
Assess radial pulse rate, strength and regularity
triggers: is the pulse strong and regular

expected.actionEn: Perform a full rapid body survey; find the wrist injury, expose it, check distal CSM and manually stabilize
triggers: head to toe for life threats
distal circulation sensation and movement in that hand

expected.actionEn: Note skin colour, temperature and condition
Check SpO2 and verbalize oxygen decision: 97% RA, titrate to keep SpO2 at or above 94%, no supplemental oxygen currently required
triggers: do I need to put him on oxygen

expected.actionEn: Keep the patient supine and still; explain why he must not move
triggers: I need you to stay still because of your neck
position of comfort is where he is
we will do the moving for you

expected.actionEn: Categorize correctly as non-RTC and manage accordingly
triggers: stable so we treat on scene

expected.actionEn: Complete spinal packaging and splinting to be ready to load within 30 minutes, working with steady purpose
Delegate partner to bring spinal device, splint kit and cot; plan the egress route through the side gate
triggers: bring the cot to the gate
we will go out through the side gate

expected.actionEn: Clarify the chief complaint (neck pain vs wrist pain) directly with the patient
triggers: is it the neck or the wrist

expected.actionEn: Obtain HxC/C using OPQRRRST plus fall critical history: height, landing surface, what hit first, LOC, cause of fall, movement since
Obtain pain scores on a 0-10 scale for both complaints
triggers: how bad is it out of 10

expected.actionEn: Obtain past medical history
Obtain medications
Obtain allergies
Obtain last oral intake with time and size
triggers: what did you eat and when

expected.actionEn: Assess GCS and verbalize component scores (E4 V5 M6 = 15)
Obtain BP by auscultation with correct cuff and stethoscope placement
Obtain pulse rate, strength and rhythm (convert to per-minute)
Obtain respiratory rate, depth and character
Physically assess skin colour, temperature, condition
triggers: back of my hand on his forehead

expected.actionEn: Assess pupils for size, equality and reactivity
Obtain SpO2 and confirm oximeter reading calibrates with palpated pulse
triggers: does the oximeter match the pulse

expected.actionEn: FE - General health and recent illness
FE - CNS: headache, dizziness, numbness, tingling, weakness (critical with spinal MOI)
triggers: any weakness in your arms or legs
can you feel your fingers and toes

expected.actionEn: FE - Respiratory system
FE - Cardiovascular system
FE - GI/GU: abdominal pain, incontinence
triggers: lost control of bladder or bowels

expected.actionEn: FE - Integumentary system
FE - Musculoskeletal system
FE - Endocrine system
FE - EENT
triggers: anything from the ears or nose

expected.actionEn: Examine head and neck (DOTS, ears/nose fluid, mouth)
Examine and auscultate chest in at least 6 sites, comparing bilaterally through inspiration and expiration
Examine abdomen (inspect and palpate four quadrants)
Examine the back during the coordinated roll, maintaining spinal alignment
triggers: checking the back during the roll
log roll and look at the back

expected.actionEn: Examine lower extremities including pelvis, with distal CSM
triggers: can you feel me touching your feet

expected.actionEn: Examine upper extremities with distal CSM comparison in both hands
triggers: can you feel this on both hands

expected.actionEn: Apply a correctly sized hard collar without losing manual stabilization
triggers: measure the neck for the collar
partner keep holding the head while I put the collar on

expected.actionEn: Package onto the spinal device: coordinated roll, neutral alignment, body strapped before head, no head tape
triggers: strap the body first then the head

expected.actionEn: Initiate the Pain Management protocol with baseline vitals done and contraindications ruled out BEFORE splinting or movement
triggers: baseline vitals are done so I can give analgesia
any liver disease or stomach bleeding
giving pain relief before we splint

expected.actionEn: Administer analgesia with the 6 rights (PCP: acetaminophen 1000 mg PO + ibuprofen 400 mg PO + Entonox; EMR: Entonox, invert cylinder 3 times)
triggers: breathe on this when the pain is bad

expected.actionEn: Splint the wrist with padding, joints above and below immobilized, cold applied 10-on/5-off, distal CSM rechecked before and after
triggers: immobilize the elbow and the hand

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs and all interventions (collar, straps, splint, distal CSM) after each major move
triggers: CSM still intact after the move
how are you doing after that move

expected.actionEn: Complete a full second set of vitals within the non-RTC interval
triggers: let us recheck the BP and pulse

expected.actionEn: Reassess pain scores after analgesia and titrate Entonox to effect
Notify the receiving hospital en route with a concise report
Deliver a complete, organized hand-off report covering all required elements
triggers: this is Mark, 34 year old male

expected.actionEn: Submit a legible, accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate moves the patient, lets or asks him to move, lift or turn his head or sit up, or applies any pain stimulus (e.g. trapezius pinch, pressing on the injured wrist) before manual in-line c-spine control is established

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) releases manual c-spine control before the patient is fully secured to the spinal device with body straps and head blocks; applying the collar alone does not permit release
Entonox is first offered or started only after the right wrist has been splinted, realigned or manipulated, or after the patient has been rolled or moved
candidate splints, realigns or manipulates the fractured wrist, or rolls or moves the patient, before any analgesia has been given
candidate finds the deformed right wrist on the rapid body survey but does not manually support or stabilize it before moving on

candidate administers a medication without asking about or examining for that medication's contraindications (Entonox: pneumothorax or chest injury, altered LOC, ability to comply; acetaminophen: liver disease, recent acetaminophen; ibuprofen: GI bleed or ulcer, anticoagulants, NSAID allergy)
candidate lets or asks the patient to sit up, stand or walk at any point in the call
candidate tapes the patient's head to the spinal device

drugs.doseEn: Inhalation, self-administered through the demand valve; titrate to effect; invert the cylinder 3 times before use
1000 mg PO (guideline range 500-1000 mg PO; may repeat once after 4 hours)
400 mg PO (guideline range 300-400 mg PO; may repeat every 4-6 hours)

Fails to initiate C-spine control at any time when indicated and/or

Does not complete baseline vital signs prior to initiating the protocol
Does not complete baseline vital signs prior to initiating the protocol

examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: You looked at the right arm during your rapid body survey - what did you see at the wrist?

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR carries no oral analgesics: pain management is Entonox only (rule out pneumothorax, ALOC, inability to comply; invert cylinder 3 times). No Functional Enquiry phase. All spinal and fracture skills are identical to PCP.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds the full 9-system Functional Enquiry and the three-drug analgesia ladder: acetaminophen 500-1000 mg PO and ibuprofen 300-400 mg PO on-boarded early, Entonox during packaging/splinting. Appendix A weighting applies: omitting Entonox when indicated after giving the oral agents, or sequencing it after fracture management, is a 100% error.

sourcePages: scenario tr-01 (data/practical/scenarios.json); BC Provincial Examination Guidelines p.7 (Findings in Unstable Adult Patients: free fall from a height > 6 m is the auto-RTC mechanism; this fall is about 4 m), p.11 (Primary Survey interventions: cervical spine stabilization when NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine indications are met), p.21 (Musculoskeletal Injuries: stabilize, check distal pulses and reassess throughout, apply cold, provide analgesia prior to movement in stable patients, immobilize the joints above and below), p.23 (cold: ice on for 10 minutes, off for 5), p.25 (Spinal Management: manual stabilization, hard collar, spinal immobilization device, foam blocks, secure the body, do not tape the head), p.58 (Acetaminophen: 500-1,000 mg PO, may repeat once after 4 hours, contraindications incl. severe liver disease and recent acetaminophen), p.65 (Entonox: contraindications incl. inability to comply, altered level of consciousness, pneumothorax; before use complete the primary survey, investigate the pain complaint incl. severity, obtain baseline vitals incl. SpO2, rule out contraindications; invert cylinder 3 X), p.68 (Ibuprofen: 300-400 mg PO, contraindications incl. active GI hemorrhage/ulcers and anticoagulants); EMALB Practical Examination Grading Criteria p.39 (Appendix A, Pain Management weighting)
